Name: The Parts of a Prompt
Desciption: Define a clear objective, offer motivation, explain the audience, give instructions, specify the output, etc.
Example: "You are an experienced product strategist. Summarize the following meeting notes into actionable insights for non-technical executives so they can prepare for an upcoming board meeting. Present the output as a concise bullet list, focusing only on product and revenue topics while excluding HR discussions. Keep it under 200 words, maintain a professional tone, and ensure each bullet clearly states the action and owner."

Name: The Human-AI Sandwich
Desciption: Let humans handle the first and last 10% (framing + final review) and AI handle the heavy middle.

Name: Let AI Become a Natural Partner
Desciption: Like you would reach for your phone to check for directions, you should reach for AI for anything related to Writing, Reasoning, Research, and Analysis.
Example:
- Try using Voice Mode or Voice to Text, can make AI fell more organic. 
- Start AI chats immediately on your phone, then continue them later from your computer.
- Some wearables (earphones, smart-watches, etc.) can connect to your AI-accounts for immediate use

Name: Treat AI as a Skill Multiplier
Desciption: AI is better at expanding your capabilities than it is at giving you completely new ones.
Example: You can ask, “Write me a sales script”. But if you can’t tell good from bad yourself, then the output is uncertain.

Name: AI Skills Compound
Desciption: the more you know (tools/techniques) the more creative you can be, and the more you will learn

Name: Upload Files
Desciption: Provide original files (PDFs, CSVs, docs) so the model can pull details from them when needed.
Example: “I’ve uploaded a 40-page research PDF. Use it as your only source to summarize the main findings in a one-page brief.”

Name: Context Formats
Desciption: Share the same context in different forms (text, screenshots, pasted tables) to improve understanding.
Example: “Here’s my spreadsheet pasted as text, and here is a screenshot of the first few rows to help you understand the structure. Help me identify trends in the sales data.”

Name: Lots of Context
Desciption: Err on the side of giving more raw material (notes, transcripts, webpage dumps, and even pictures/screenshots) when unsure what’s needed.
Example: “Here are my messy project notes and meeting transcripts. Please extract the main decisions, open questions, and owner for each action item.”

Name: Prune Irrelevant Information
Desciption: Remove obviously unrelated content so the model isn’t distracted or misled.
Example: “Here’s our project doc with the HR section removed. Based only on the product-related content, outline the next 5 milestones.”

Name: Structure Context
Desciption: Organize inputs into labeled sections like BACKGROUND, GOAL, CONSTRAINTS, EXAMPLES.
Example: “BACKGROUND: … GOAL: … CONSTRAINTS: … EXAMPLES: … Using this structure, propose a launch plan for the next 30 days.”

Name: Use AI to Pre-Process Context
Desciption: First ask the model to summarize or reorganize large, messy inputs into compact, structured notes.
Example:
Prompt 1: “Here are 20 pages of notes. Summarize them into a concise outline with headings and bullet points.”
Prompt 2: “Turn that outline into a 2-page strategy memo.”

Name: Define Output Structure
Desciption: Describe the exact fields and columns you want the model to return.
Example: “Return a markdown table with these columns: ‘Feature’, ‘User Segment’, ‘Value Proposition’, ‘Risk Level (Low/Med/High)’.”

Name: Provide Examples
Desciption: Show a model answer and tell the AI to follow that style and structure. Note: Experiment with this, because the model can often copy the example too closely.
Example: “Here is an example performance review paragraph. Using this style and tone, write a review for an engineer with the following achievements: …”

Name: Break into Sub-Steps
Desciption: Decompose big tasks into smaller steps (outline A & B → draft A → draft B).
Example:
Prompt 1: “Create an outline for a 10-slide pitch deck.”
Prompt 2: “Write the voice track for slide 1.”
Prompt 3: “Write the speaker notes for slide 1.” 
…

Name: Itterate
Desciption: Run iterative cycles (draft → refine → repeat).
Example:
Prompt 1: “Draft a 1-page proposal”
Prompt 2: “Rewrite it to be 20% shorter and more persuasive.”

Name: Self-Itterate
Desciption: Have the model critique its own output and propose improvements.
Example: “1) Identify the weaknesses and missing details of your last response. 2) Rewrite incorporating your own feedback.”

Name: Draft in a Canvas
Desciption: Use a dedicated drafting space (canvas / doc) for long-form content to make editing easier.
Example: “Write a detailed project plan in a pop-out canvas, including sections for Objectives, Scope, Timeline, and Risks.”

Name: Ask for Assumptions
Desciption: Require the model to explain its assumptions, reasoning steps, and approach.
Example:
Prompt 1: “Don’t answer yet. First, explain your assumptions and the method you’ll use.”
Prompt 2: “A better interest rate to use is 8%, and assume the interest is applied monthly. Now tell me the answer.”

Name: Request Multiple Options
Desciption: Have the model generate several options with pros/cons so you can choose.
Example: “Give me 3 different positioning statements for this product, with pros and cons for each and a recommendation.”

Name: Trigger Self-Critique
Desciption: Ask the model to play devil’s advocate and challenge its own conclusions.
Example: “You just recommended Option B. Now play devil’s advocate and argue why Option B might fail and what we should watch for.”

Name: Show Its Work
Desciption: Instruct the model to think through the problem step-by-step before responding. Note: This is especially important for non-reasoning models.
Example: “Talk through your reasoning step by step before giving a final answer: Is this A/B test design statistically sound?”

Name: Think Very Long and Hard
Desciption: Add this for extra computation. Note: This only works on reasoning models.
Example: “Think very long and hard and design an algorithm to allocate budget across channels under these constraints and justify your approach.”

Name: Use a Thinking Model
Desciption: Use a reasoning-focused model when accuracy and logical depth matter most.
Example: “Analyze this legal clause for ambiguities and outline possible interpretations and risks.”

Name: Use an Instant Model
Desciption: Use a faster model for bulk, repetitive, or low-risk tasks.
Example: “Convert this unstructured log of customer complaints into a 1000-row table with columns for ‘Customer’, ‘Issue Category’, and ‘Sentiment’.”

Name: Structure Data
Desciption: AI can turn unstructured text into a structure (e.g. table, JSON, etc.)
Example: "Turn the text of this web page into a markdown table with the following headers: Product Name, Price, & Description"

Name: Reformat Data
Desciption: AI can intellegently refactor or reformat data
Example: "Take all of the names and put them into Lastname, Firstname format."

Name: Internal Analysis
Desciption: Using Python, AI can run calculations or generate figures.
Example: "Using our historic growth data, project when we will double in size. Plot our projected growth curve over top of the historic data."

Name: External Analysis
Desciption: AI can help you run analysese, by generating Excel / Google Sheet formulas.
Example: "Help me develop an excel formula that will calculate the corellation coeficient between sales commision percentage and closing rate."

Name: Internal Capabilities
Desciption: Using Python, AI can do simple actions: Generate a QR code, convert image types, add headers or page numbers to PDFs, etc.
Example: "Combine these two PDFs and add page numbers to the bottom right of the pages in Arial 12pt. font."

Name: Debugging and Trouble Shooting
Desciption: AI can walk you through complex problems if you upload screenshots, pictures, or error codes.
Example: "Here is a screenshot of my computer. Where did the menue bar go, and how do I get it back?"

Name: Turn Chats into Reusable Prompts
Desciption: Convert successful conversations into general, reusable prompts.
Example: “Analyze this conversation where you helped me design a workshop. Draft a reusable prompt that would recreate this kind of workshop plan for any topic.”

Name: Parameterize Your Prompts
Desciption: Add variables like {{Audience}}, {{Tone}}, and {{Length}} so prompts can be reused easily.

Name: Organize a Prompt Library
Desciption: Maintain a catalog of your best prompts by use case and domain.

Name: Add Verification Instructions
Desciption: Explicitly tell the model to flag uncertainty or speculation.
Example: “Answer these questions and label each statement as ‘Confident’, ‘Likely’, or ‘Speculative’. Highlight anything that needs human verification.”

Name: Require Checkable Sources
Desciption: Ask the AI to provide verifiable sources for factual claims.  Note: make sure to check them, because sources can also be hallucinated.
Example: “Provide a short answer to this question and list 3 credible sources I can check. Clearly separate facts from your own inferences.”

Name: Self-Check for Errors
Desciption: Ask the model to check its own answers for accuracy. Note: Reasoning models often do this automatically if you include "Think very long and hard" to the prompt.
Example: “Check your summary against the source text and look for any inconsistencies, serious omissions, or contradictions.”

Name: Clear Chat History
Desciption: AI can be biased by prior chat history (in this conversation and, if ‘History’ is turned on, in others). Start a new chat if the quality seems to be decreasing.  Note: You can restart from earlier in the same chat thread.

Name: Sanity-Check Math
Desciption: Double-check all numerical and statistical output, especially when the model is not reasoning (e.g. “Analyzing…”).

Name: Validate Data Sources
Desciption: Confirm that inputs are accurate and well-parsed, especially from messy or OCR’d sources.

Name: Avoid Plagiarism
Desciption: AI may mimic phrasing from training data. Always edit, add original thinking, and run checks where required.
Example: “Use this article as inspiration, but write an original blog post in my voice and mention 3 places where I should add personal anecdotes.”

Name: Remove Sensitive Data
Desciption: Avoid including personal, confidential, or regulated information unless you’re in a compliant setup.
Example: “Here is anonymized customer feedback (names and IDs removed). Analyze key themes and suggest product improvements.”

Name: Disclose AI Assistance
Desciption: Be transparent about AI involvement where compliance, ethics, or expectations require it.

Name: Don’t Delegate High-Risk Decisions
Desciption: Use AI for analysis and options, not final calls in legal, medical, financial, or HR decisions.
Example: “Summarize the pros and cons of these contract clauses and list questions I should ask my lawyer before signing.”
